case_name: Sarguja Transport Service v State Transport Appellate Tribunal, M.P., Gwalior
respondent:
State Transport Appellate Tribunal, M.P., Gwalior
Supreme Court of India

12 November 1986
Special Leave Petition (Civil) No. 5665 of 1986
The Judgment was delivered by : E. S. Venkataramiah, J.
On the expiry of the period of a permit : to run a stage carriage on the route Jashpurnagar Ambikapur issued under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (hereinafter referred to as ' the Act') in favour of the Janta Transport Co-operative Society. the petitioner and some
facts: On the expiry of the period of a permit to run a stage carriage on the route Jashpurnagar Ambikapur issued under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') in favour of the Janta Transport Co-operative Society.
The petitioner and some others filed applications for the grant of the said permit before the Regional Transport Authority, Bilaspur.
The Janta Transport Co-operative Society also made an application for the renewal of the permit in its favour.
The application for renewal filed by the Janta Transport Co-operative Society was rejected by the Regional Transport Authority on the ground that it was barred by time.
On a consideration of the relative merits of the other applicants, namely. the petitioner and others, the Regional Transport Authority granted the permit in favour of the petitioner.
issues: The effect of the withdrawal of a writ petition filed under Articles 226/227 of the Constitution of India without the permission of the High Court to file a fresh petition.

Whether the petitioner was precluded from instituting any fresh suit in respect of the same subject-matter or part of the claim after abandoning the earlier suit or withdrawing it without the permission of the Court.
petitioner_arguments: The main contention urged before this Court by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the High Court was in error in rejecting the writ petition out of which this case arises, on the ground that the petitioner had withdrawn the earlier writ petition in which he had questioned the order passed by the Tribunal on 4.10.1985 without the permission of the High Court to file a fresh petition.
respondent_arguments: It is urged by the learned counsel that since the High Court had not decided the earlier petition on merits but only had permitted the petitioner to withdraw the petition, the withdrawal of the said earlier petition could not have been treated as a bar to the subsequent writ petition.
court_reasoning: The principle underlying rule 1 of Order XXIII of the Code is that when a plaintiff once institutes a suit in a Court and thereby avails of a remedy given to him under law, he cannot be permitted to institute a fresh suit in respect of the same subject-matter again after abandoning the earlier suit or by withdrawing it without the permission of the Court to file fresh suit.
The Code as it now stands thus makes a distinction between 'abandonment' of a suit and 'withdrawal' from a suit with permission to file a fresh suit.
holding: Accordingly, the petition is dismissed summarily.
